answer_1.quote: We design a two-step summarization framework that takes the FINDINGS (F) section of a radiology report ... and produces an IMPRESSIONS (I) section ... Our DiMAC summarization model can outperform existing baseline models for text summarization.
datasets: Radiology reports from Princeton Radiology and University medical centers (English)

answer_2.quote: We follow standard practice and evaluate the quality of generated IMPRES‑SIONS by comparing against ground‑truth IMPRES‑SIONS using ROUGE. ... sentence reward r_as^j is computed using R1 (ROUGE unigram recall).

answer_4.quote: To assess the overall quality and factual correctness of the IMPRESSIONS generated by DiMAC, we obtained evaluations from two board‑certified radiologists. ... For each measure, we asked the radiologists to score the summary as 1, 2 or 3 for bad, borderline or good.
answer_4.guideline: Radiologists rated each generated IMPRESSIONS on two measures: (1) overall quality and (2) factual correctness and completeness, using a 1‑3 Likert scale.
